## Overview

In pressurized micro-irrigation systems (drip and micro-sprinkler), spatial pressure variation along a lateral pipe directly governs water application uniformity. Because discharge decreases stepwise at each emitter outlet, friction head loss along the lateral is non-linear.

`calc_backstep()` implements the **backstep numerical procedure**: starting from a known boundary pressure head at the distal emitter, it steps upstream segment by segment toward the lateral inlet. You can choose the head loss equation from the `hf` package via `method` (`"darcy"`, `"flamant"`, or `"hw"`) and specify the volumetric flow rate unit directly with `flow_unit` (such as `"m3/s"`, `"L/s"`, or `"L/h"`).

```{r load-packages}
library(irritool)
library(ggplot2)

```

---

## 1. Level Lateral Line (`slope = 0`) and Flow Units (`flow_unit`)

Consider a polyethylene drip lateral with internal diameter $D = 0.012\text{ m}$ ($12\text{ mm}$), absolute roughness $\varepsilon = 1.5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}$, and $50$ emitters spaced at $0.30\text{ m}$ intervals.

Emitter discharge follows $q = k \cdot H^x$ with discharge coefficient $k = 3.18\text{ L h}^{-1}\text{ mca}^{-x}$ and exponent $x = 0.50$. By setting `flow_unit = "L/h"`, there is no need to manually convert the emitter coefficient to $\text{m}^3\,\text{s}^{-1}$, and both `emitter_flow` and `section_flow` are returned directly in $\text{L h}^{-1}$. Assuming a target distal pressure head of $10\text{ mca}$:

```{r flat-lateral}
level_profile <- calc_backstep(
  end_pressure = 10,
  diameter = 0.012,
  spacing = 0.30,
  n_emitters = 50,
  slope = 0,
  emitter_coef = 3.18,
  emitter_exp = 0.50,
  method = "darcy",
  flow_unit = "L/h",
  roughness = 1.5e-6
)

head(level_profile)
tail(level_profile)

```

Inlet operating pressure head and total lateral inlet flow rate are retrieved from the first row (`emitter == 1`):

```{r inlet-summary}
# Required inlet pressure head (mca)
level_profile$pressure_head[1]

# Total inlet flow rate (L/h)
level_profile$section_flow[1]

```

---

## 2. Effect of Terrain Slope (`slope`)

The `slope` parameter specifies elevation change per unit length ($\text{m m}^{-1}$):

* **Positive values** (`slope > 0`) represent uphill flow (elevation gain toward the distal end).
* **Negative values** (`slope < 0`) represent downhill flow (elevation drop toward the distal end).

```{r slope-comparison}
uphill_profile <- calc_backstep(
  end_pressure = 10,
  diameter = 0.012,
  spacing = 0.30,
  n_emitters = 50,
  slope = 0.02,
  emitter_coef = 3.18,
  emitter_exp = 0.50,
  flow_unit = "L/h",
  roughness = 1.5e-6
)

downhill_profile <- calc_backstep(
  end_pressure = 10,
  diameter = 0.012,
  spacing = 0.30,
  n_emitters = 50,
  slope = -0.02,
  emitter_coef = 3.18,
  emitter_exp = 0.50,
  flow_unit = "L/h",
  roughness = 1.5e-6
)

comparison_df <- rbind(
  cbind(level_profile, scenario = "Level (0%)"),
  cbind(uphill_profile, scenario = "Uphill (+2%)"),
  cbind(downhill_profile, scenario = "Downhill (-2%)")
)

ggplot(comparison_df, aes(x = emitter, y = pressure_head, color = scenario)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Pressure Head Profile Along Lateral Line",
    x = "Emitter Index (1 = Lateral Inlet)",
    y = "Pressure Head (mca)",
    color = "Slope Scenario"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

```

---

## 3. Comparing Head Loss Equations (`method`)

In addition to Darcy-Weisbach (`method = "darcy"`, default), `calc_backstep()` supports the Flamant (`method = "flamant"`) and Hazen-Williams (`method = "hw"`) empirical equations, forwarding equation-specific parameters (such as `roughness` or `coef`) through `...`:

```{r method-comparison}
flamant_profile <- calc_backstep(
  end_pressure = 10,
  diameter = 0.012,
  spacing = 0.30,
  n_emitters = 50,
  slope = 0,
  emitter_coef = 3.18,
  emitter_exp = 0.50,
  method = "flamant",
  flow_unit = "L/h",
  coef = 0.000135
)

hw_profile <- calc_backstep(
  end_pressure = 10,
  diameter = 0.012,
  spacing = 0.30,
  n_emitters = 50,
  slope = 0,
  emitter_coef = 3.18,
  emitter_exp = 0.50,
  method = "hw",
  flow_unit = "L/h",
  coef = 140
)

methods_df <- rbind(
  cbind(level_profile, method = "Darcy-Weisbach"),
  cbind(flamant_profile, method = "Flamant (b = 0.000135)"),
  cbind(hw_profile, method = "Hazen-Williams (C = 140)")
)

ggplot(methods_df, aes(x = emitter, y = pressure_head, color = method)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Comparison of Head Loss Equations Along Lateral Line",
    x = "Emitter Index (1 = Lateral Inlet)",
    y = "Pressure Head (mca)",
    color = "Equation"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

```
